question: In a logic circuit, two inputs A and B are applied to an AND gate, and the output of the AND gate is connected to the input of a NOT gate. If the inputs A and B are both at logic 0, what will be the output of the entire circuit?
solution:
The correct answer is __1**(Logic High)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Logic Circuit Analysis__ is essential to understanding the behavior of gates.
 
• An AND gate outputs 1 (Logic High) only when both inputs are 1.
 
• If inputs A and B are both 0, the output of the AND gate will be 0 (Logic Low).
 
• The output of the NOT gate will be the inverse of the AND gate's output. NOT(0) = 1.
 
• Thus, the final output of the circuit is 1 (Logic High).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **AND Gate:**

 
 
• Outputs 1 only when both inputs are 1.
 
• Truth table: A=0, B=0 → Output=0; A=1, B=1 → Output=1.
 
 
 
• **NOT Gate:**
 
 
• Inverts the input signal.
 
• Truth table: Input=0 → Output=1; Input=1 → Output=0.
 
 
 
• **Logic Gates Combination:**
 
 
• Combining gates allows complex circuit functionalities.
 
• Output depends on input logic and gate arrangement.
